title: Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable
abstract: Möbius RoPE is a rotary positional encoding built on the anti-periodic frequency ladder $θ_i=π(2i+1)/N$: every rotation plane advances by an odd multiple of $π$ across the training context, so the positional holonomy is $-1$ and the two ends of the sequence are deterministically coupled through a closed-form Dirichlet "dipole"; to our knowledge this is the first anti-periodic boundary condition in positional encoding. We verify the theory numerically to $\sim 10^{-6}$ and pretrain 48 models spanning six 160M-class and three 410M-class arms (2B FineWeb-Edu tokens each; the hybrid arm puts Möbius frequencies on 25% of heads). Hybrid perplexity is unchanged (29.66 vs. 29.72), but needle-in-a-haystack retrieval becomes reliable: $90.3\pm5.7\%$ versus $63.3\pm31.4\%$ at context 512 ($n=6$ seeds), observed worst seed 86% versus 14%, robust variance tests $p=0.013$-$0.029$ (unadjusted), recurring at 410M (Levene $p=0.040$). Matched controls isolate the mechanism: an aperiodic ladder in the same frequency band reproduces none of the effect, and a periodic (holonomy $+1$) ladder only a fraction. Swapping trained models' frequency table back to standard RoPE (weights frozen) collapses retrieval, with damage concentrated on far needles: trained models depend on this long-range geometry. A NoPE arm is even more reliable at short context but pays a 13% perplexity tax and extrapolates worst; only the anti-periodic hybrid pairs baseline perplexity with a high reliability floor. The effect is scoped to single-needle retrieval within the training window; a one-line frequency swap thus provides zero-cost insurance against the retrieval seed lottery.

The effect is scoped to single-needle retrieval within the training window; a one-line frequency swap thus provides zero-cost insurance against the retrieval seed lottery. keywords: positional encoding , rotary position embedding , in-context retrieval , training stability , anti-periodic boundary condition , language model pretraining \affiliation [aff1]organization=JRTI, city=Seoul, postcode=05855, country=Republic of Korea 1 Introduction Whether a pretrained language model can retrieve a fact planted earlier in its context is one of the most consequential capabilities that emerges (or fails to emerge) during pretraining. We find experimentally that at small scale this capability is subject to a severe seed lottery : six 160M-class (162M-parameter) models pretrained identically with standard RoPE, differing only in random seed, span needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) accuracies from 14% to 98% at a context of 512 tokens (§ 5.2 ). Perplexity gives no warning: the retrieval-failing seeds are not worse language models (correlation between perplexity and retrieval across the 12 RoPE-vs-hybrid models is only + 0.206 +0.206 ; across the study’s 30-model five-arm cohort the association even runs against quality, § 5.3 ). A practitioner who trains one model and sees healthy loss curves has no way to know whether the resulting model retrieves reliably or not. This paper proposes a deterministic geometric intervention that largely eliminates this lottery. Standard RoPE (Su et al., 2024 ) rotates each two-dimensional query/key plane of a d h d_{h} -dimensional attention head at frequency θ i = 10000 − 2 ​ i / d h \theta_{i}=10000^{-2i/d_{h}} ; these frequencies share no short common period, so at large relative distance the per-plane phases scramble and the positional inner product wanders erratically. We ask: what if positions lived on a circle with an anti-periodic boundary condition (the condition obeyed by fermionic fields, whose allowed modes are the half-integer harmonics)? Setting θ i = π ​ ( 2 ​ i + 1 ) / N \theta_{i}=\pi(2i+1)/N , every rotation plane advances by an odd multiple of π \pi after N N positions, so the composite rotation after one full traversal is exactly − I -I : the positional holonomy is − 1 -1 . This has three closed-form consequences (§ 3 ): (i) the position-only attention profile is a Dirichlet kernel that is essentially silent over the interior of the sequence (largest interior response ≤ 2.2 % {\leq}2.2\% of the endpoint response at d h = 64 d_{h}{=}64 ); (ii) the two ends of the context are deterministically coupled with a sign flip, an end-to-end dipole (informally, a “wormhole” between the sequence boundaries); and (iii) under length extrapolation the positional coefficient remains bounded and exactly 2 ​ N 2N -periodic, in contrast to standard RoPE’s aperiodic phase drift. We verify each prediction numerically to ∼ 10 − 6 {\sim}10^{-6} . Anti-periodicity is a strong prior, so we do not impose it everywhere. Our hybrid scheme gives Möbius frequencies (with N N fixed to the training context, 2048) to 25% of attention heads and standard RoPE to the rest, adding zero parameters and zero FLOPs: it is literally a different constant table of sines and cosines for a quarter of the heads. Contributions. 1. A new class of positional encoding. We introduce anti-periodic boundary conditions into positional encoding, with closed-form theory (Dirichlet-kernel attention signature, − 1 -1 holonomy, dipole structure, bounded 2 ​ N 2N -periodic extrapolation), verified numerically to ∼ 10 − 6 {\sim}10^{-6} (§ 3 , § 3.4 ). 2. Main empirical result: retrieval reliability. In n = 6 n{=}6 -seed pretraining runs at 160M/2B tokens, hybrid Möbius RoPE matches standard RoPE’s perplexity (29.66 vs. 29.72) while raising mean NIAH accuracy at every in-training length (suggestive, not individually significant; min p = 0.09 p=0.09 ) and, more importantly, collapsing its across-seed variance: raw ratio 30.8 × 30.8\times at L = 512 L{=}512 , robust variance tests p = 0.013 p=0.013 – 0.029 0.029 , worst seed 86% vs. 14% (§ 5.2 ). The variance reduction replicates at 410M with n = 4 n{=}4 per arm (SD 6.5% vs. 16.5% at L = 2048 L{=}2048 , Levene p = 0.040 p=0.040 ; worst seed 29.4% vs. 18.8%) (§ 5.4 ). 3. The active ingredient is anti-periodicity, isolated by controls and made causal by ablation. Two matched control pretraining arms ( n = 6 n{=}6 each) dissect the mechanism: an aperiodic ladder covering the identical low-frequency band (no holonomy class) reproduces none of the reliability effect (variance ratio 1.0 × 1.0\times vs. standard), and a periodic ladder (integer harmonics, holonomy + 1 +1 ) only a fraction ( 3.1 × 3.1\times , n.s.); against 30.8 × 30.8\times for holonomy − 1 -1 , this is a dose–response ordering in the boundary condition. An evaluation-time ablation on the trained hybrid models (all weights frozen, only the frequency table swapped back to standard) collapses retrieval from 90.3 % 90.3\% to 41.7 % 41.7\% at L = 512 L{=}512 , with damage concentrated on far-from-query needles ( − 55 -55 pp at depth 0.1 vs. − 36 -36 pp at depth 0.9): trained models causally depend on the Möbius geometry, with the damage pattern implicating its long-range structure (§ 5.3 ). 4. A reliability–quality trade-off across positional-encoding families. A NoPE arm ( n = 6 n{=}6 ; no positional encoding) achieves the best short-context retrieval reliability of all arms ( 95.2 ± 4.0 % 95.2{\pm}4.0\% at L = 512 L{=}512 , worst seed 88.8%), but pays a 13 % 13\% perplexity tax (33.66 vs. 29.66–29.72), redevelops a seed lottery at the full training length (SD 24.1% at L = 2048 L{=}2048 vs. hybrid’s 8.2%), and extrapolates worst ( 5.6 × 5.6\times ppl blow-up at 4 ​ N max 4N_{\max} ). Across the 30 models of the five-arm cohort, retrieval and language-modeling quality anti-align ( r = + 0.43 r{=}{+}0.43 between ppl and NIAH, p = 0.017 p{=}0.017 , pooled across arms); hybrid Möbius is the only arm that combines standard-level perplexity with a high, low-variance retrieval floor (§ 5.3 ). 5. A capacity–scale interaction in allocating the anti-periodic budget. Splitting the Möbius heads across multiple scales (“ladder”, N ∈ { 512 , 1024 , 2048 } N\in\{512,1024,2048\} ) is significantly worse than a single scale at 160M ( − 30 -30 pp, p = 0.015 p=0.015 ; dipole dilution); yet at 410M ( n = 4 n{=}4 per arm) the ordering reverses: ladder attains the best mean NIAH at every length with the smallest seed-variance among the n = 4 n{=}4 arms, and the best extrapolation perplexity ( ppl \mathrm{ppl} @4096 35.7 vs. 38.7, Welch p = 0.006 p=0.006 ; all four seed-paired deltas negative, paired p = 0.013 p=0.013 ). Concentrate the budget when heads are scarce; distribute it when heads are plentiful (§ 5.5 ). 6. A characterized failure boundary. Beyond the training length, all variants collapse to 0% retrieval through the same critical transition (median retrieved-token rank jumps from ∼ 2.5 {\sim}2.5 – 6 6 to ∼ 8 , 400 {\sim}8{,}400 – 9 , 500 9{,}500 between L = 2048 L{=}2048 and 3072 3072 ; needle attention mass evaporates 0.073 → 0.004 0.073\to 0.004 at 3072, 0.003 0.003 by 4096) (§ 5.6 ). Möbius RoPE is for reliable retrieval within the training window , not a long-context method (§ 6 ). Practical framing. The intervention is a one-line frequency change on 25% of heads with no cost at the training length: pretraining insurance that converts a capability that emerges stochastically into one that emerges reliably. 2 Related Work Rotary positional encoding. RoPE (Su et al., 2024 ) encodes relative position by rotating query/key pairs in d h / 2 d_{h}/2 two-dimensional planes at geometrically spaced frequencies θ i = b − 2 ​ i / d h \theta_{i}=b^{-2i/d_{h}} (base b = 10 4 b=10^{4} ). Because the θ i \theta_{i} share no short common period, the encoding is aperiodic in practice: no shift of realistic length returns the phase configuration to itself, and long-range relative phases are effectively scrambled. All of our comparisons use this standard parameterization as the baseline. Length generalization for RoPE. A large body of work modifies RoPE’s frequency spectrum to extend usable context: position interpolation (Chen et al., 2023 ) , NTK-aware scaling and YaRN (Peng et al., 2024 ) , LongRoPE (Ding et al., 2024 ) , FoPE’s Fourier-series spectrum repair (Hua et al., 2025 ) , and MrRoPE’s mixed-radix generalization (Tian et al., 2026 ) . Our goal is orthogonal: we do not extend context. We change the boundary condition at a fixed training length, and show explicitly (§ 5.6 ) that our method does not help, and slightly hurts, beyond the training window. Among non-rotary families, we pretrain a NoPE arm (Kazemnejad et al., 2023 ) under the identical protocol as a reference point outside the RoPE family (§ 5.3 ); ALiBi (Press et al., 2022 ) is left to future work. All within-family comparisons are against standard RoPE, the dominant choice in current pretrained models. Periodic positional encodings. The closest relative is P-RoPE (Huo, 2026 ) , which pairs sliding-window attention with a periodic positional structure (positions are reset modulo the window, so the encoding returns to itself after one traversal, holonomy + 1 +1 in our terms). Anti-periodic frequencies are a topologically distinct class (half-integer harmonics, holonomy − 1 -1 ; within the class of N N -(anti)periodic encodings the two holonomy classes are separated, though generic non-periodic ladders interpolate between them), and the sign matters: holonomy + 1 +1 aliases the two ends of the sequence, whereas − 1 -1 couples them with a deterministic sign flip; this is the distinction between a cylinder and a Möbius band. To our knowledge no prior positional encoding uses anti-periodic boundary conditions (prior-art search: July 2026). Möbius structures in attention. MöbiusAttention (Halacheva et al., 2024 ) introduces Möbius transformations (complex fractional-linear maps) into the attention computation, acting on learned query/weight representations to enrich their geometry. Despite the shared name, it is unrelated to our construction: it modifies the attention nonlinearity with learned projective maps, whereas we modify the positional boundary condition with a fixed, parameter-free frequency ladder. Our “Möbius” refers to the − 1 -1 holonomy of the position bundle, i.e., the topology of the Möbius band. Retrieval evaluation and emergence. Passkey retrieval (Mohtashami & Jaggi, 2023 ) , popularized as needle-in-a-haystack testing (Kamradt, 2023 ) , is commonly applied to pretrained models at long context; we use it instead as a probe of whether the capability emerges at all during small-scale pretraining, across seeds. The instability we document connects to induction heads (Olsson et al., 2022 ) ; our results suggest that at small scale the formation of such retrieval circuitry is seed-dependent. Our intervention can be read as seeding that circuit geometrically. Physics antecedents. Our ladder is exactly the Matsubara mode structure of fermionic fields on a thermal circle ( ω n = π ​ ( 2 ​ n + 1 ) / β \omega_{n}=\pi(2n+1)/\beta ; Matsubara, 1955 ; the fermionic anti-periodicity condition itself: Ezawa et al., 1957 ), with inverse temperature replaced by context length; we import the boundary condition, not any dynamical content. 3 Theory: Anti-Periodic Frequencies and the Dipole Kernel 3.1 Setup RoPE acts on a head of dimension d h d_{h} (even) by partitioning it into P = d h / 2 P=d_{h}/2 planes and rotating plane i i of the query/key at position m m by angle m ​ θ i m\theta_{i} : R ​ ( m ) = ⨁ i = 0 P − 1 ( cos ⁡ m ​ θ i − sin ⁡ m ​ θ i sin ⁡ m ​ θ i cos ⁡ m ​ θ i ) , q m = R ​ ( m ) ​ q , k n = R ​ ( n ) ​ k , R(m)=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{P-1}\begin{pmatrix}\cos m\theta_{i}&-\sin m\theta_{i}\\ \sin m\theta_{i}&\cos m\theta_{i}\end{pmatrix},\qquad q_{m}=R(m)\,q,\quad k_{n}=R(n)\,k, (1) so that ⟨ q m , k n ⟩ \langle q_{m},k_{n}\rangle depends only on the relative offset m − n m-n . Every linear positional feature built from these frequencies (any fixed linear combination of the per-plane sines and cosines) is anti-periodic, f ​ ( m + N ) = − f ​ ( m ) f(m+N)=-f(m) , and 2 ​ N 2N -periodic; periodic constructions ( R ​ ( N ) = + I R(N)=+I ) cannot distinguish position m m from m + N m+N , while the anti-periodic class distinguishes them by sign. 3.3 Closed-form attention signature: a Dirichlet kernel Consider the pure positional geometry: identical, per-plane-normalized query and key ( q = k q=k , equal energy in every plane). The position-only attention coefficient at offset m m is the average phase coherence c ​ ( m ) = 1 P ​ ∑ i = 0 P − 1 cos ⁡ ( m ​ θ i ) = 1 P ​ ∑ i = 0 P − 1 cos ⁡ ( ( 2 ​ i + 1 ) ​ x ) , x = π ​ m N . c(m)\;=\;\frac{1}{P}\sum_{i=0}^{P-1}\cos\!\big(m\,\theta_{i}\big)\;=\;\frac{1}{P}\sum_{i=0}^{P-1}\cos\!\big((2i+1)\,x\big),\qquad x=\frac{\pi m}{N}. The kernel is a dipole : + 1 +1 lobe at offset 0, − 1 -1 lobe at offset N N , near-zero in between; under this diagnostic ( q = k q=k , equal per-plane energy), a key at one end contributes a deterministic pre-softmax coefficient of ≈ − 1 {\approx}{-}1 at the other end. The sign is benign: the coupling enters pre-softmax, where a sign flip of the learned key projection converts inhibition to excitation. 4. (P4) Bounded, 2 ​ N 2N -periodic extrapolation. For any runtime length L L , c c is exactly given by the same formula; | c | ≤ 1 |c|\leq 1 always, c ​ ( m + N ) = − c ​ ( m ) c(m+N)=-c(m) , c ​ ( m + 2 ​ N ) = c ​ ( m ) c(m+2N)=c(m) . Standard RoPE trivially satisfies | c | ≤ 1 |c|\leq 1 as well, but admits no analogous closed form or short exact period: its coefficient at fixed offset drifts quasi-randomly, with no 2 ​ N 2N -periodic structure. 3.4 Numerical verification All four predictions were tested directly (Phases 1–2.5 on CPU/MPS; Stage A on H100): 1. Attention-map signature (Phase 1). N × N N\times N attention maps under Möbius frequencies match the Dirichlet closed form with maximum absolute error 1.33 × 10 − 6 1.33\times 10^{-6} (5/5 registered predictions pass), including the sign-flipped anti-diagonal corner (Fig. 2 , appendix). 2. End-to-end signal transport (Phase 2; Fig. 4 ). In a single attention layer at N = 10 , 000 N=10{,}000 , a value vector planted at position 0 is transported, sign-inverted, to position N − 1 N{-}1 with cos ⁡ ( o , V ) = − 0.9606 \cos(o,V)=-0.9606 : one-hop propagation across ten thousand tokens through the negative dipole lobe. Implementation cost is unchanged (only the constant cos/sin table differs; measured runtime versus sequence length matches the standard-RoPE implementation, log–log slope 1.002). 3. Dipole profile census (Phase 2.5; Fig. 5 ). Full profile scan at N = 10 , 000 N=10{,}000 , D = 32 D=32 confirms a silent bulk (largest middle-50% response = = 4.2% of the endpoint response, matching the closed form’s 4.2%; 2.2% at D = 64 D=64 ) with extremal negative response exactly at the far end (argmin at position 0 as predicted); 3/3 pass. 4. Extrapolation (Stage A; Fig. 3 ). With θ i \theta_{i} frozen at N max = 2048 N_{\max}=2048 , the measured endpoint coefficient c ​ ( L ) c(L) at the ten registered runtime lengths L ∈ { 0.25 , … , 4 } × N max L\in\{0.25,\dots,4\}\times N_{\max} (up to 8192) matches theory with per-point error ≤ 1.8 × 10 − 6 \leq 1.8\times 10^{-6} (max over the full 800-point float32 sweep: 1.2 × 10 − 5 1.2\times 10^{-5} ); it is bounded and 2 ​ N max 2N_{\max} -periodic (e.g., c ​ ( L − 1 ) = − 0.9984 c(L{-}1)=-0.9984 at L = 2048 L=2048 and + 0.0022 +0.0022 at L = 2560 L=2560 , i.e., offsets 2047 and 2559), while the standard-RoPE coefficient varies erratically ( + 0.20 +0.20 , + 0.24 +0.24 , + 0.014 +0.014 , − 0.011 -0.011 , …) with no closed form. All four registered judgments pass. Why might a dipole help retrieval? Retrieval circuits must learn to move information from an arbitrary earlier position to the current query; under standard RoPE the long-range positional geometry is unstructured, and whether training discovers such a circuit appears to be seed-dependent (§ 5.2 ). The Möbius dipole provides the network with a deterministic long-range channel at initialization ; the hypothesis tested below is that this scaffold makes retrieval-circuit formation reliable rather than left to chance. 4 Method: Hybrid and Ladder Head Allocation Anti-periodicity trades bulk positional resolution for boundary coupling, so imposing it on all heads is likely harmful for language modeling. We therefore use mixed allocations: Hybrid (main method). A fraction ρ = 0.25 \rho=0.25 of attention heads (deterministically the first ⌈ ρ ​ H ⌉ \lceil\rho H\rceil heads of every layer) use Möbius frequencies with a single N max = 2048 N_{\max}=2048 equal to the training context; the remaining 75% use standard RoPE ( b = 10 4 b=10^{4} ). For the 160M model ( H = 12 H=12 ) this is 3 Möbius heads per layer; for 410M ( H = 16 H=16 ), 4 heads. No new parameters; the only change is the cos/sin table applied to those heads. FLOPs, memory, and throughput are identical to the baseline. Ladder (ablation). To test whether multi-scale dipoles help, the ladder variant assigns 3 heads per layer Möbius frequencies with different scales N max ∈ { 512 , 1024 , 2048 } N_{\max}\in\{512,1024,2048\} (one head per scale, a positional “skip list” of dipoles), the rest standard. This probes whether several weaker boundary couplings at staggered ranges beat one strong coupling at the full context scale. The ladder always uses 3 Möbius heads: at 160M this matches hybrid’s budget (3/12), but at 410M it is 3/16 ( ρ = 18.75 % \rho{=}18.75\% ) vs. hybrid’s 4/16 ( ρ = 25 % \rho{=}25\% ), so the 410M ladder-vs-hybrid comparison confounds allocation with a slightly smaller budget. Controls (mechanism dissection). Anti-periodicity confounds two ingredients: where the frequencies live (a narrow low-frequency band) and how they are quantized (half-integer harmonics, holonomy − 1 -1 ). Two matched control allocations separate them, each identical to hybrid except for the special heads’ frequency table: band uses a geometric, mutually incommensurate ladder spanning exactly the Möbius band [ π / N , π ​ ( d h − 1 ) / N ] [\pi/N,\,\pi(d_{h}{-}1)/N] : same band placement, no holonomy class ( R ​ ( N ) ≠ ± I R(N)\neq\pm I ); periodic uses integer harmonics θ i = 2 ​ π ​ ( i + 1 ) / N \theta_{i}=2\pi(i{+}1)/N (the nearest integer-harmonic band, [ 2 ​ π / N , π ​ d h / N ] [2\pi/N,\,\pi d_{h}/N] , one frequency bin from the Möbius band), with holonomy + 1 +1 (the cylinder to Möbius’s band). Together with hybrid (holonomy − 1 -1 ) they dissect band placement from boundary condition across three boundary classes. NoPE and mobius (all-heads). A NoPE arm (no positional encoding on any head) is pretrained under the identical protocol as an out-of-family reference (§ 5.3 ); all-heads mobius is used only in the synthetic suite (§ 5.1 ). 5 Experiments All pretraining uses one pipeline: decoder-only transformers (GPT-NeoX tokenizer), FineWeb-Edu (Penedo et al., 2024 ) streamed and packed, sequence length 2048, 2.0B tokens (3814 steps × \times 524,288 tokens), AdamW, lr 6 × 10 − 4 6\times 10^{-4} cosine, bf16, H100. Two pythia-like scales (Biderman et al., 2023 ) : 160M (12 layers, d model = 768 d_{\text{model}}{=}768 , 12 heads) and 410M-class (405M parameters; 24 layers, d model = 1024 d_{\text{model}}{=}1024 , 16 heads); d h = 64 d_{h}=64 for both. Same-seed runs within a training round share identical data order, so same-round within-seed comparisons are paired (the control arms used a mirrored data-serving path; limitation 9); seed-paired tests corroborate the independent-samples tests reported below (e.g., paired t t at L = 512 L{=}512 , hybrid vs. standard: p = 0.110 p=0.110 , vs. Welch p = 0.090 p=0.090 ). Evaluation. (i) Validation perplexity at 2048 and extrapolated lengths 4096/8192 (training-time validation losses and these evaluation perplexities are computed on different held-out samples of the stream and are not numerically interchangeable). Causal ablation: trained models need the geometry. We take the six trained hybrid models and, at evaluation time only, (i) swap the Möbius heads’ frequency table back to standard RoPE with all weights frozen ( rope-swap ), (ii) zero the Möbius heads’ output projection ( zero-mob ), or (iii) zero an equal number of standard heads ( zero-std , damage control). Rope-swap, which changes no parameters, collapses retrieval from 90.3 ± 5.7 % 90.3{\pm}5.7\% to 41.7 ± 26.9 % 41.7{\pm}26.9\% at L = 512 L{=}512 (and 90.0 → 28.1 % 90.0\to 28.1\% at 256, 55.0 → 32.8 % 55.0\to 32.8\% at 1024), on every seed. Depth-resolved, the damage concentrates on needles far from the query ( − 55.2 -55.2 and − 58.9 -58.9 pp at depths 0.1 and 0.3, easing to − 36.5 -36.5 pp at depth 0.9): the trained circuit depends most on the removed geometry in the far half of the context, where query–needle distances are longest, consistent with the Möbius planes’ low-frequency long-range structure (of which the endpoint dipole is the extreme case). This establishes causal dependence on the anti-periodic geometry; attributing it to the endpoint lobe specifically rests on the closed form and this distance pattern, and remains partly interpretive. We caution that the head-zeroing conditions are less diagnostic: zero-std collapses retrieval even harder ( 7.2 % 7.2\% at 512), i.e., removing any 3 of 12 heads from these small models is catastrophic, so the causal weight rests on rope-swap, which removes nothing but the geometry. Task-scope probe: the reliability effect is specific to single-needle retrieval. To test generality beyond passkey NIAH, we evaluated all 30 archived checkpoints on two harder retrieval families under the identical protocol (trial-paired across models; 160 trials per length each): KV-lookup (4–12 key–value pairs planted in filler; query one key’s value) and multi-needle (three named passkeys; query one by name). Both tasks sit near the capability floor at this scale (arm means 2.5–25.6% at L ∈ { 512 , 1024 } L\in\{512,1024\} ), and no arm, hybrid included, reproduces the variance-collapse signature there (all Levene tests n.s.; hybrid attains the best RoPE-family means on both tasks, + 4.5 +4.5 pp KV and + 8.4 +8.4 pp multi-needle at L = 512 L{=}512 , but n.s. at n = 6 n{=}6 ; NoPE’s mean advantage partially generalizes, + 10.4 +10.4 pp multi-needle, p = 0.026 p=0.026 ). Two readings fit these results: floor compression limits variance comparisons (the mirror image of the NIAH ceiling caveat), and, consistent with the mechanism, the dipole is a positional end-to-end channel, not a content-addressing device: it reliably transports a single planted signal across the context, but provides neither key → \to value binding (KV) nor disambiguation among same-format competitors (multi-needle). The reliability claim of this paper is therefore scoped to the single-needle regime that the geometry actually addresses. The NoPE surprise, and the trade-off. The out-of-family NoPE arm is the most reliable short-context retriever in the study ( 95.2 ± 4.0 % 95.2{\pm}4.0\% at L = 512 L{=}512 ; flat depth profile 92.7–96.9%, consistent with purely content-based addressing), evidence that the seed lottery is largely induced by positional structure interfering with retrieval-circuit formation . However, this reliability comes at a cost on every other axis: (i) it pays a 13% perplexity tax at the training length (33.66 vs. 29.66–29.72; final val loss 3.474 vs. 3.333), (ii) its reliability is confined to short/mid context: at L = 2048 L{=}2048 its own lottery re-emerges (SD 24.1% vs. hybrid’s 8.2%), and (iii) it extrapolates worst of all arms ( ppl \mathrm{ppl} ratio 5.60 × 5.60\times at L = 8192 L{=}8192 vs. standard’s 3.89 × 3.89\times ). Across the 30 models of the five-arm control cohort (ladder excluded) the pattern generalizes: perplexity and NIAH@512 are positively correlated ( r = + 0.431 r{=}{+}0.431 , p = 0.017 p{=}0.017 ; a pooled, between-arm association, as within-arm samples are too small to establish a model-level trade-off), i.e., worse language models retrieve more reliably. This exposes a trade-off surface across positional-encoding families on which hybrid Möbius is the only arm that pays neither cost: standard-RoPE perplexity and a near-NoPE reliability floor within the training window (band matches the perplexity without the reliability; NoPE the reliability without the perplexity). 5.4 Scaling to 410M-class models (405M parameters) Round 2 repeats the comparison at 405M parameters/2B tokens (seeds 0–1; all three arms were later extended to n = 4 n{=}4 , seeds 0–3; for the Möbius arms see § 5.5 ).
